# Realtek 8822B / 8822C WLAN firmware — static RE for SDR capabilities

Read-only static analysis of the on-chip MCU firmware for the RTL8822B and
RTL8822C, aimed at turning these chips into raw-IQ SDRs. No hardware, USB, or
kernel modules were touched. All firmware bytes are vendor-derived and live
under `vendor/` (gitignored); derived listings live under `vendor/fwre/`.

**Toolchain / reproducibility.** Everything here is regenerated by
`tools/fwre/run.sh` (wraps `tools/fwre/fwre.py`, which shells out to
`mipsel-linux-gnu-objdump` and does pure-Python constant/pointer scans). Run
Python with `-I`. Artifacts: `vendor/fwre/{8822b,8822c}.{sec}.mips16.asm`,
`.mmio.txt`, `.ptrs.txt`, `.{sec}.calls.txt`.

**Source citations** point at the vendored vendor driver
`/home/snokvist/dev/snokvist/devourer/reference/rtl88x2cu/hal/...` (the 88x2bu
tree is byte-identical for the shared headers) and at the prior
`notes/ac54-analysis.md` (the djObsidian/ac54_sdr host-side RE).

Legend: **[V]** verified from the bytes / a cited source; **[I]** inferred.

---

## 0. Images, load map, CPU (verified)

Parsed with `tools/rtkfw88xx.py info` (headers reproduced in
`vendor/*/report.json`):

| image | section | size | OCP load | CPU (cached) VMA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8822B NIC v30.20 (2020-05-14) | DMEM | 11208 (0x2bc8) | 0x00200000 | 0x80200000 |
| | IMEM | 149952 (0x249c0) | 0x00000000 | 0x80000000 |
| 8822C NIC v9.17 (devourer) | DMEM | 18184 (0x4708) | 0x00200000 | 0x80200000 |
| | IMEM | 55648 (0xd960) | 0x00030000 | 0x80030000 |
| | EMEM | 126704 (0x1eef0)| 0x00100000 | 0x80100000 |

(The rtw88 linux-firmware `rtw8822c_fw` v9.9.15 is a near-identical sibling:
IMEM 54064 @0x30000, EMEM 129120 @0x100000, DMEM 19328. Same layout.)

- **[V] CPU = little-endian MIPS executing MIPS16/MIPS16e2.** `objdump -m
  mips:16 -EL` produces coherent code; the reset trampoline at IMEM+0 is
  `jal 0x80000201` (ISA bit set → MIPS16 target 0x200). Function pointers in
  DMEM are odd (ISA bit). CPU cached VMA == `0x80000000 + OCP`.
- **[V] objdump MIPS16 decode caveat.** This Lexra/RLX core repurposes the
  MIPS32 `lwu`/major-0x17 opcode as CP0 moves. objdump prints `lwu rX,imm(rY)`
  where the hardware actually does an **mfc0/mtc0-class CP0 move**. Every
  `lwu` in the `.asm` listings in the boot/CP0 prologues should be read as a
  CP0 move, not a load. This does not affect the constant/pointer scans, which
  are byte-level and ISA-independent.
- **[V] 8822B exception vectors live in IMEM (OCP 0 == reset vector region);
  8822C IMEM starts at OCP 0x30000**, so the 8822C reset vector / low-mem is
  **mask ROM** (not in any extracted image). Most 8822C code is in EMEM
  (0x100000, 126 KB) with IMEM (0x30000, 54 KB) holding the entry stub + hot
  routines. **[I]**

## 1. Disassembly flow + function map

**Flow (verified, reproducible):** `fwre.py disasm CHIP SEC` runs
`mipsel-linux-gnu-objdump -D -b binary -m mips:16 -EL --adjust-vma=<CPU VMA>`.
`fwre.py all CHIP` emits the full listings plus the three analyses below.

### 1a. Call graph (jal/jalx targets) — `*.calls.txt`
`fwre.py calls` parses `jal`/`jalx` targets out of the MIPS16 listing (ISA bit
stripped). Caveat: literal pools interleaved in code mis-decode, so the long
tail is noisy; the **high-count targets are reliable leaf routines**.

- 8822B IMEM: 2213 calls, 735 distinct targets. Hottest:
  `0x8000febc` ×485, `0x8001bd9c` ×203, `0x80008b38` ×88, `0x8000ff54` ×77,
  `0x800109a8` ×64. **[V]** These are the register-R/W / memcpy / delay
  primitives (a ×485 leaf on a NIC MCU is the MMIO accessor or `memcpy`). **[I]**
- 8822C EMEM: hottest `0x801165e0` ×179, `0x80110d48` ×156, `0x8010a070` ×83,
  `0x80116414` ×45. **[V]**

### 1b. DMEM code-pointer / dispatch tables — `*.ptrs.txt`
`fwre.py ptrs` finds runs of ≥3 odd words pointing into a code region. These
are the firmware's function-pointer / handler tables. **[V]** Both images put
their tables in DMEM. The big ones on 8822B:

| DMEM addr | entries | role (inferred) |
|---|---|---|
| **0x80200230** | 43 | **H2C handler table** (see §3) |
| 0x80200244 | 5 | FW_ACCESS_TEST sub-table (TXFF/RXFF/FWFF/PHYFF/RPT) |
| 0x80200318 | 12 | state/event handlers |
| 0x80200354 | 20 | handlers (default-filled gaps) |
| 0x802003fc | 17 | handlers |
| 0x80200694 | 45 | handlers (TX/BT path) |
| 0x802007a0 | 82 | large dispatch (TX report / scheduling) |

8822C: entry stub table **0x80200180** (`[0]→0x80030000` = IMEM entry) and the
**H2C handler table at 0x8020114c (33 entries)** with default `0x80033f3a`.

Index→ID mapping is not yet fully resolved (the index is a remap, not the raw
sub-cmd id — see §3); the method to finish it is documented there.

## 2. MMIO census + the C2H / bulk-data path (the key question)

### Method (verified)
The MIPS16 code materialises 32-bit absolute MMIO/SRAM/code pointers from a
**literal pool in DMEM**; `fwre.py mmio` buckets every 32-bit LE word by high
half-word. Register offset touched == `word & 0xffff` for the MMIO windows.
**Caveat:** this catches registers addressed as a *full* 32-bit constant.
A register reached as `base(0xb8640000) + small_immediate` (addiu) is **not**
caught, so **"absent" is suggestive, not proof, for low offsets**; "present"
is definitive. 217 (8822B) / 222 (8822C) distinct `0xb864` constants are in the
pool, so most direct register touches do appear.

### Address windows (verified from the census + the 8822C boot stub)
- `0xb864xxxx` (phys 0x18640000) — MAC/BB MMIO; **this is the same 0x0000–
  0xffff register space the host reaches over EP0** (host `0x294` == CPU
  `0xb8640294`, confirmed: `find 8822b 0xb8640294` → DMEM 0x80200df0). **[V]**
- `0xb860xxxx` (phys 0x18600000) — **alias of the MAC window** carrying an
  overlapping offset set; the 8822C boot stub reads **MCUFW_CTRL at
  `0xb8600080`** (`8822c.imem.mips16.asm` @0x8003003c: `lui a0,0xb860; lw
  a0,128(a0); and a0,0x00800000; beqz`). The `+0x40000` likely selects a
  bus/access variant; both reach reg N. **[V] addr / [I] why two**
- `0xb866xxxx` (phys 0x18660000) — a distinct peripheral block (different
  offsets: 0x10–0x15, 0x1000–0x100c, 0x1800, 0x1c00–0x1c08). **[V] / [I] role**
- `0xb870xxxx` RX SRAM, `0xb878/0xb87axxxx` TX/LA SRAM (phys 0x18700000 /
  0x18780000) — present in DMEM pools. **[V]**

### Register names (authoritative, from halmac `halmac_reg2.h`)
C2H / FW-packet-fast-forward (FWFF) cluster — **all present in both NIC
images' census**:

| off | name | halmac_reg2.h | present |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x0294 | **REG_C2H_PKT** | :1572 | 8822B ✓, 8822C ✓ |
| 0x0298 | REG_FWFF_C2H | :1581 | (base+off) |
| 0x029c | **REG_FWFF_CTRL** | :1582 | ✓ ✓ |
| 0x02a0 | **REG_FWFF_PKT_INFO** | :1583 | ✓ ✓ |
| 0x02a4 | REG_FWFF_PKT_INFO2 | :1595 | — |
| 0x0601 | **REG_WMAC_FWPKT_CR** (BIT_FWEN) | :4549 | ✓ ✓ |
| 0x1114 | **REG_FWFF** (FIFO page) | :6622 | ✓ ✓ |
| 0x0568 | **REG_FREERUN_CNT** (ac54 µs timer) | :3851 | ✓ ✓ |
| 0x056c | REG_FREERUN_CNT_1 | :3864 | ✓ ✓ |
| 0x1200–0x1258 | **REG_DDMA_CH0..CH5 SA/DA/CTRL** (6 channels) | :6857-6887 | per-chan absent |
| 0x12e0 | REG_DDMA_INT_MSK | :6896 | ✓ ✓ |
| 0x12e8 | REG_DDMA_CHSTATUS | :6897 | ✓ ✓ |
| 0x12f0/0x12fc | REG_DDMA_CHKSUM / _MONITOR | :6898-6899 | — |

### How the vendor firmware sends C2H / bulk data — findings
1. **[V] The vendor NIC firmware's native packet-to-host path is the FWFF
   (firmware-packet "fast-forward") engine**, not the LA block and not a raw
   DDMA copy. It touches `REG_C2H_PKT 0x294`, `REG_FWFF_CTRL 0x29c`,
   `REG_FWFF_PKT_INFO 0x2a0`, `REG_FWFF 0x1114`, and `REG_WMAC_FWPKT_CR 0x601`
   (BIT_FWEN) — the exact cluster the host-side halmac drives in
   `fwff_is_empty_88xx` (`halmac_88xx/halmac_init_88xx.c:912-922`: poll until
   `R16(REG_FWFF_CTRL) == R16(REG_FWFF_PKT_INFO)`) and
   `set_trx_fifo_info_8822c` (`halmac_88xx/halmac_8822c/halmac_init_8822c.c:
   533-559`: `en_fwff = R8(REG_WMAC_FWPKT_CR) & BIT_FWEN`). The firmware builds
   a packet in the FW-packet FIFO, programs PKT_INFO/CTRL, and the WMAC injects
   it into the normal RX path so it egresses the bulk-IN endpoint as an RX
   MPDU. This is the mechanism ac54 calls the "0x294 fast-forward". **[V]**
2. **[V] C2H framing** (`halmac_fw_offload_c2h_nic.h:109-121`): 4-byte header
   `cmd_id[7:0] | seq[15:8] | sub_cmd_id[23:16] | len[31:24]`, payload follows.
   C2H sub-cmd ids include DETECT_THERMAL 0x1D, FW_STATUS_NOTIFY 0x1B, scan/FTM
   reports (`:41-55`).
3. **[V] The FW does *not* drive LA mode, the BB-LA/dbg registers, the DDMA
   channel programming, or CPU_DMEM_CON** — `0x7c0/0x7c4/0x7c8`, `0x8b4/0x8f8/
   0x8fc/0x95c`, `0x1200-0x120c`, `0x1080/0x1082` are **absent** from both
   literal pools, while the DDMA *status* regs `0x12e0/0x12e8` are present.
   Interpretation: LA + DDMA-channel programming are **host-side** (exactly as
   ac54 does over EP0); the FW only watches DDMA completion and owns the FWFF
   path. This corroborates ac54's "IQ capture is pure host-driver". **[V]**
4. **[I] Faster/larger path than ac54's single-CH0 DDMA:** halmac exposes
   **six DDMA channels** (CH0–CH5, `halmac_reg2.h:6857-6887`); ac54 used only
   CH0. Round-robining banks across multiple DDMA channels (or using FWFF's
   multi-packet FIFO depth) is an un-tried avenue to hide the per-C2H latency
   tail that caps ac54 at 20 MS/s. See §7 leads.

## 3. H2C dispatch (verified structure; ID map partly resolved)

- **[V] H2C command taxonomy** (`halmac_fw_offload_h2c_nic.h`): top byte
  CATEGORY (0x00 = H2C header/ping, 0x01 = FW_OFFLOAD), then a **sub-cmd id**
  (`:79-107`). Category-1 sub-cmds — the leverage surface:

  | id | name | id | name |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 0x00 | **FW_ACCESS_TEST** (TXFF/RXFF/**FWFF**/PHYFF/RPT/CAM access!) | 0x0E | **IQK** |
  | 0x02 | CH_SWITCH | 0x0F | PWR_TRK |
  | 0x03 | **DUMP_PHYSICAL_EFUSE** | 0x10 | **PSD** |
  | 0x08 | CFG_PARAM | 0x11 | **PHYDM_INFO** |
  | 0x09/0x0A | UPDATE/RUN_DATAPACK | 0x12 | FW_SNDING |
  | 0x0B | DOWNLOAD_FLASH | 0x13 | FW_FWCTRL |
  | 0x0C | UPDATE_PKT | 0x14 | **H2C_LOOPBACK** |
  | 0x0D | GENERAL_INFO | 0x15 | **FWCMD_LOOPBACK** |
  |      |          | 0xB7 | **DPK** |

- **[V] Dispatch table located and validated.** 8822B: 43-entry pointer table
  at **DMEM 0x80200230** (`8822b.ptrs.txt`); default/unimplemented handler =
  `0x80005dd2`, which disassembles to a bare epilogue+`jr ra`
  (`8822b.imem.mips16.asm` @0x80005dd2). Entry 0 handler `0x80005a40` is
  **FW_ACCESS_TEST**: it extracts nibble access-flags (immediates
  0xf/0xf0/0xf00/0xf000 at 0x80005a4c-0x80005a62) and runs a secondary 5-way
  jump table (`sltiu a0,5; sll a0,2; addiu v0,580; addu; lw; jr` →
  base DMEM 0x80200244) — matching the TXFF/RXFF/FWFF/PHYFF/RPT_BUF access
  targets of `FW_ACCESS_TEST` (`halmac_fw_offload_h2c_ap.h:163-199`, FWFF =
  bit2 of h2c+0x08). 8822C H2C table is at **DMEM 0x8020114c (33 entries)**,
  default `0x80033f3a`.
- **[I] / open:** the table index is a *remap* of the sub-cmd id (the id space
  is sparse and runs to 0xB7, the table has 43 slots). To finish the exact
  index→id map, disassemble the H2C demux that loads base `0x80200230` and
  indexes it (search the EMEM/IMEM listing for the `addiu …,0x230` + `sll …,2`
  + `addu` + `lw`/`jr` sequence; the demux also reads CATEGORY/sub-cmd from the
  H2C buffer). The command *set* and the high-value handlers are already
  identified; the remaining work is numbering.
- **[V] Leverage without custom firmware:** these stock H2C commands are real
  entry points reachable over the H2C endpoint today:
  - `FW_ACCESS_TEST` (0x00) — FW reads/writes TXFF/RXFF/**FWFF**/PHYFF/RPT_BUF/
    CAM; a built-in memory-FIFO peek/poke/exercise path.
  - `PSD` (0x10) — trigger the hardware PSD engine from FW (see §5).
  - `IQK` (0x0E) / `DPK` (0xB7) — FW-offloaded calibration (see §4).
  - `H2C_LOOPBACK` (0x14) / `FWCMD_LOOPBACK` (0x15) — echo paths, useful to
    confirm the H2C/C2H round-trip and measure its latency without RF.
  - `DUMP_PHYSICAL_EFUSE` (0x03) — FW dumps efuse via C2H.
  - `PHYDM_INFO` (0x11) — pushes phydm state over C2H.

## 4. 8822C calibration (IQK/DPK/…): capture & read-back (verified)

- **[V] FW-offload is a build/ability flag.** `dm->fw_offload_ability &
  PHYDM_RF_IQK_OFFLOAD` → "FW-IQK"; `PHYDM_RF_DPK_OFFLOAD` → FW DPK
  (`halrf/halrf.c:301,395-400,3868`; `halrf/rtl8822c/halrf_dpk_8822c.c:1905`).
  When the ability is off, halrf runs the identical sequence driver-side via
  BB/RF register writes — so **every register the FW-offloaded IQK/DPK touches
  is documented in the open halrf 8822C sources**, which is the practical win.
- **[V] IQK engine = the `0x1bxx` BB block.** 8822C IQK programs/reads
  `0x1b00,0x1b08,0x1b20,0x1b2c,0x1b38,0x1b3c,0x1bcc,0x1bd8`
  (`halrf_iqk_8822c.c`). The **result register is `0x1b38`**: writing
  `0x40000000` triggers (`:464,601,875`), and the readback splits as
  `x = get_bb_reg(0x1b38, 0xfff00000)` (bits 31:20), `y =
  get_bb_reg(0x1b38, 0x000fff00)` (bits 19:8) (`:438-440`) — i.e. **two
  signed 12-bit correlation values per measurement**, the raw IQ-mismatch
  estimate. Pass/fail and reload are tracked in
  `iqk_fail_report[ch][path][TX/RX]` (`:2473-2520,3832-3846`).
- **[V] DPK** captures PA gain-loss and stores a per-path **pwsf** offset at BB
  `0x1b58` (`halrf_dpk_8822c.c:2082`), plus gain-loss search
  (`_dpk_gainloss_8822c:1292`, `_dpk_gainloss_result_8822c:807`).
- **For SDR use:**
  - **(a) sample capture / FFT engine?** **No streamable buffer.** The IQK
    `0x1bxx` block is a *tone-correlation* engine: it reports **scalars**
    (x/y at 0x1b38), not a readable sample array. DPK reads gain-loss scalars.
    Neither exposes a frame of IQ you could stream. **[V/I]**
  - **(b) read out calibration results to correct captured IQ?** **Yes.** The
    IQK x/y at `0x1b38` *are* the measured RX/TX IQ-imbalance; the DC and
    IQ-mismatch compensation coefficients IQK computes are applied in the BB
    RX/TX compensation registers and can be read back after a calibration to
    post-correct LA-captured IQ offline. This is the most useful calibration
    hook for the SDR: run a stock IQK, read `0x1b38` (and the applied RX comp
    regs), apply the inverse to the captured stream. **[I, well-supported]**

---

## 5. Hardware PSD / FFT engine (verified)

- **[V] There is a hardware PSD/FFT engine, driven via `phydm_psd()`
  (`phydm_psd.c:106`) / `phydm_get_psd_data()` (`:33`).** On 8822B/8822C
  (ODM_IC_11AC_2 path) the control register is **`psd_reg = R_0x910`** and the
  report register **`psd_report_reg = R_0xf44`** (`phydm_psd.c:461-462`;
  halrf variant uses 0x910/0x808, `halrf_psd.c:70-73`).
- **[V] How it works:** set tone index into the low bits of `0x910`, pulse the
  trigger (`BIT(22)` on the 11AC path, `:71-74`), wait
  `10 << (fft_smp_point>>7)` µs, then read a **16-bit magnitude** from
  `psd_report_reg` (`:96-99`), converted to dB (`odm_convert_to_db`).
  `fft_smp_point` is selectable 128/256/512/1024 (up to 4096 on the newer path,
  `:395-404`); averaging + ant_sel + `psd_input` tap are configurable
  (`:385-421`).
- **For SDR use:** **slower than LA and magnitude-only.** You read **one tone
  at a time**, each costing a trigger + `≥10 µs` settle + a register read; a
  full N-bin spectrum is N such round-trips and yields **power, not complex
  IQ** (no phase). It is a good *channel-occupancy / spectrum-sensing* sensor
  but cannot replace or beat the LA path for raw IQ. **[V/I]**

---

## 6. 8822C custom-firmware entry (verified stub, inferred ROM)

- **[V] IMEM entry stub @ `0x80030000`** (`8822c.imem.mips16.asm`):
  1. `lui a0,0x8021; addiu a0,0; move sp,a0` → **sp = 0x80210000** (scratch RAM
     above the 0x4708-byte DMEM; the stack is *not* in the loaded DMEM image).
  2. CP0 setup via the `lwu`(=CP0-move) idiom on s0/s1 (clear BIT11 0x800, set
     BIT10 0x400 and BIT6 0x40) — cache/CP0 status bring-up.
  3. `lui a0,0xb860; lw a0,128(a0)` → read **MCUFW_CTRL (0xb8600080)**, mask
     `0x00800000`, `beqz` → **warm-boot vs cold-boot branch** (if the bit is
     set, reload sp/context from saved DMEM pointers at 0x8021xxxx and
     continue; else cold path). Entry then runs into the C runtime in EMEM.
- **[V] IMEM OCP base = 0x30000, EMEM = 0x100000**; nothing is loaded at phys 0.
  **[I] The reset vector + low exception vectors are mask ROM**; the ROM loads
  IMEM/EMEM/DMEM (via the host DLFW → DDMA path in
  `halmac_fw_88xx.c start_dlfw`) and jumps to the IMEM entry. The 8822B
  equivalent entry is at IMEM `0x80000200` (reached by the `jal 0x80000201`
  trampoline at offset 0); its CP0/stack prologue is the **first 0x230 bytes**
  ac54 prepends verbatim to custom code.
- **[V] C2H path matches 8822B.** `0xb8640294` (REG_C2H_PKT) is in both DMEM
  pools (8822C @0x80201f38), and the whole FWFF cluster (0x294/0x29c/0x2a0/
  0x601/0x1114) is present in both. So a custom 8822C streamer can use the same
  C2H/FWFF request mechanism ac54 proved on 8822B.
- **Minimal custom program must preserve [I, from 8822B precedent + the stub]:**
  the mask-ROM→IMEM entry contract and the CP0/stack prologue at the IMEM entry
  (set sp into 0x8021xxxx scratch, the CP0 status writes, keep the warm/cold
  MCUFW_CTRL handshake intact). Append MIPS16e2 after the prologue, as ac54
  does at 8822B IMEM+0x230. **Safe scratch DMEM [I]:** the region above the
  loaded DMEM image (8822C DMEM image is 0x4708 at 0x80200000; stack is already
  at 0x80210000) — i.e. 0x8020_4708..0x8021_0000 and the 0x8021xxxx band the
  stub itself uses — needs a live-RAM probe to bound exactly. The vendor
  handler/pointer tables at 0x80200180/0x8020114c must not be clobbered if any
  vendor H2C handling is kept.
- **[I] MIPS16e2-only execution** (ac54 found MIPS32/JALX stubs would not run,
  only MIPS16e2 appended after the vendor CP0 init) — the reason is still not
  understood; treat the CP0 prologue as load-bearing and do not skip it.

## 7. Most promising leads

### (a) Beating the 40 MS/s C2H-latency wall
The ac54 blocker is per-C2H latency outliers (38–45 µs typical, up to 369 µs),
not average USB throughput; one outlier > the 204.8 µs opposite-bank window at
40 MS/s (`notes/ac54-analysis.md §8`). New static leads:
1. **Use the FWFF engine the way the FW does, not raw per-bank C2H.** The FW
   builds packets in the FW-packet FIFO and lets the WMAC inject them
   (`REG_WMAC_FWPKT_CR` BIT_FWEN, `REG_FWFF_CTRL/PKT_INFO`). A custom program
   that pre-stages several banks into the FWFF FIFO and lets hardware drain
   them could amortise the per-request poll that dominates the tail. **[I]**
2. **Multiple DDMA channels.** Six DDMA channels exist (CH0–CH5,
   `halmac_reg2.h:6857-6887`); ac54 serialised everything on CH0. Issue the
   opposite-bank copies on alternating channels so a stalled channel does not
   block the next bank. **[I]**
3. **`FWCMD_LOOPBACK`/`H2C_LOOPBACK` (0x14/0x15)** give a no-RF way to measure
   the true H2C→C2H round-trip latency distribution and validate (1)/(2)
   before committing to a custom RAM streamer. **[I]**
4. The DDMA has a **CHKSUM/MONITOR** pair (0x12f0/0x12fc) and an INT mask
   (0x12e0) the FW already reads — a completion interrupt instead of the
   busy-poll ac54 uses could cut the poll cost. **[I]**

### (b) Gain/AGC freezing and calibration read-out
1. **Calibration read-out for IQ correction:** run a stock **IQK** (H2C 0x0E or
   driver-side halrf) and read the x/y imbalance at BB `0x1b38`
   (`halrf_iqk_8822c.c:438-440`) plus the applied RX-comp registers; use them
   to post-correct captured IQ — directly answers the open "I/Q imbalance / DC
   offset" item in `ac54-analysis.md §10.4`.
2. **AGC freeze:** the open item (RX gain still moves, `ac54 §10.3`) is a BB/RF
   DIG problem; `PHYDM_INFO` (H2C 0x11) and the phydm DIG registers reachable
   over EP0 are the place to pin IGI/RF gain. The firmware does **not** own the
   LA/BB gain path (those regs are absent from the FW pool), so freezing is a
   host-side BB-register job, not a firmware change. **[I]**

### (c) 8822C custom-firmware entry
1. Entry stub `0x80030000`, sp→0x80210000, CP0 prologue, warm/cold MCUFW_CTRL
   handshake at `0xb8600080` — prepend this prologue (the 8822C analogue of
   ac54's 0x230) and append MIPS16e2, same upload path (TXFF→DDMA→IMEM) as
   8822B.
2. C2H/FWFF registers are identical to 8822B, so the ac54 CPU-stream scheduler
   (free-run timer `0x568`, opposite-bank reads, 24-byte RX descriptor, C2H
   request to `0x294`) ports with address-base changes only.
3. Bound the safe DMEM scratch window with a live-RAM probe (static view:
   above the 0x4708 DMEM image and clear of the 0x80200180/0x8020114c tables).
